title: Presentations of flat formal hypersurface deformations
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n\geq1$, and let $0\ne f\in(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^2\subset k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $R$ be a commutative Artinian local $k$-algebra with residue field $k$; Artinian means the descending chain condition on ideals. Let $Q$ be a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra, flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], with a specified isomorphism $Q/\mathfrak m_RQ\cong k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]/(f)$. For any lifts $q_i\in\mathfrak m_Q$ of the specified classes of $x_i$, substitution gives a continuous surjection $R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\twoheadrightarrow Q$ and its kernel has a generator $F$ reducing to $f$. Conversely, for every lift $F$ of $f$, the quotient $R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]/(F)$ is flat over $R$. For a surjection $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ of such Artinian algebras, a flat lift $Q'$ of $Q$, and a specified presentation $Q=R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]/(F)$, the coordinates and generator can be lifted so that $Q'=R'[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]/(F')$ with $F'\bmod\ker(R'\to R)=F$, respecting the specified reduction isomorphism. These choices may be made compatibly along any tower $R/\mathfrak m_R^j$ for a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra $R$: a compatible system of flat hypersurface deformations is given by one equation in $R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$. The module representing continuous relative derivations of this quotient into complete finitely generated modules is the cokernel of the Jacobian column $(\partial F/\partial x_i)_i:Q\to Q^{\oplus n}$. Moreover, if $R$ is a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra, $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $x\in X$ is a point over the closed point with an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]/(F)$, then $\Omega_{X/R,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$, with $\Omega$ the relative Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], is the cokernel of the Jacobian column $(\partial F/\partial x_i)_i$ over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$.

source.place: Tag 0DY5 (lemma-power-series-rings-TI), proof of (2), the lifted-equation presentation; the Artinian-base and compatible-tower version is the same presentation argument using flatness and complete Nakayama. Continuous differential presentation is the universal-derivation Jacobian calculation. These extensions are stated by the worker, not quotations of the first-order lemma.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R$ and $B=R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$. The Artinian-local lemma gives that $R$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak m^N=0$; hence $R$ is complete, since its quotient tower is eventually constant. The power-series Noetherianity, local-ring and combined-ideal completeness results show that $B$ is Noetherian local and complete for $J=\mathfrak mB+(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. Coefficient reduction identifies $B/\mathfrak mB$ with $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$: its kernel is $\mathfrak mB$ by the cited coefficient-kernel result, and it is onto by lifting each coefficient. The same Noetherianity, locality and completeness assertions hold for a complete Noetherian local base $R$, with this same $J$.

source.place: Tags 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0), 00J8 (lemma-artinian-radical-nilpotent), 0306 (lemma-Noetherian-power-series); coefficientwise completion and reduction as in the cited power-series nodes

proof.text: The prescribed $q_i\in\mathfrak m_Q$ define an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:B\to Q$ by the power-series universal property, using the assumed maximal-ideal completeness of $Q$. It is continuous for the maximal-ideal topologies: $\mathfrak m$ has nilpotent image in $Q$, so maps into $\mathfrak m_Q$, and $\phi(J^r)\subseteq\mathfrak m_Q^r$. Modulo $\mathfrak m$, the composite with the specified special-fibre isomorphism is precisely the quotient map $k[[x]]\to k[[x]]/(f)$, by the coordinate prescription. Thus $B/\mathfrak mB\to Q/\mathfrak mQ$ is onto. Nilpotent Nakayama applied to the $R$-linear map $\phi$ gives surjectivity of $\phi$; no finite generation of $Q$ as an $R$-module is needed.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (11), applied to the substitution in Examples of Deformation Problems Tag 0DY5 (lemma-power-series-rings-TI), proof (2)

proof.text: Put $K=\ker\phi$. Tensor $0\to K\to B\to Q\to0$ with $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Since its last term $Q$ is $R$-flat, the cited flat-quotient tensor lemma makes $K/\mathfrak mK\to B/\mathfrak mB$ injective with image exactly $(f)$. Choose $F\in K$ mapping to the element $f$ of this ideal. Then $K=BF+\mathfrak mK$. Apply nilpotent Nakayama over $B$ to $B\to K$, $b\mapsto bF$, with nilpotent ideal $\mathfrak mB$. This gives $K=BF$, and therefore the asserted presentation with precisely the prescribed reduction of its generator.

source.place: Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero) and Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (11); expanded flatness argument in Examples of Deformation Problems Tag 0DY5, proof (2)

proof.text: Conversely, the constants map $R\to B$ is flat by the power-series constants-flatness result, and is local by Step 1. The ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ is a domain by the power-series domain result. Thus $0\ne f\in(x)^2$ is a nonzerodivisor and a nonunit, so is a length-one regular sequence. For any coefficient lift $F$ of $f$, apply the regular-sequence lifting theorem to the flat local map $R\to B$: it gives both that $F$ is a nonzerodivisor in $B$ and that $B/(F)$ is $R$-flat. Its quotient is complete Noetherian local by the complete-local quotient theorem. This argument also applies over a complete Noetherian local base with the same specified residue field and special-fibre equation.

Let $I=\ker(R'\twoheadrightarrow R)$, $B'=R'[[x]]$, and fix the given identification $Q'/IQ'=Q$. Lift each specified coordinate $q_i$ to $q'_i\in Q'$. These lifts are in the maximal ideal, since $IQ'$ is nilpotent and the quotient is local. Step 2 gives $B'\twoheadrightarrow Q'$ with kernel $K'$. Coefficient reduction gives $B'/IB'=B$. Tensor $0\to K'\to B'\to Q'\to0$ over $R'$ with $R$; flatness of $Q'$ identifies $K'/IK'$ with the kernel $(F)$ of the specified $B\to Q$. In particular $F$ itself lifts to $F'\in K'$. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_{R'}$ is nilpotent, nilpotent Nakayama applied to $B'\to K'$, $b\mapsto bF'$, gives $K'=(F')$. Both coordinates and the exact equation $F$, rather than just its ideal, now have the required reductions. The diagram commutes on coefficients and variables, hence on series by the substitution universal property.

source.place: Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero) and Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK); relative version of the lifted-equation argument of Examples of Deformation Problems Tag 0DY5

proof.text: For a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra $R$ with residue field $k$, write $R_j=R/\mathfrak m_R^j$ for $j\ge1$. These are Artinian local by the cited quotient theorem. A compatible system here includes reduction isomorphisms $Q_{j+1}\otimes_{R_{j+1}}R_j\cong Q_j$ satisfying their cocycle identities, and the specified special-fibre identification. Begin with $Q_1=k[[x]]/(f)$, its standard coordinates, and $F_1=f$. Inductively apply Step 5 to $R_{j+1}\to R_j$, the specified reduction of $Q_{j+1}$, and the already chosen presentation of $Q_j$. It chooses coordinates and $F_{j+1}$ reducing exactly to the preceding ones. This is an induction with fixed base and successor data, so all presentations commute with every transition map.

source.place: Tag 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0), applied to the maximal-ideal-power quotients; agent induction using Step 5

proof.text: Set $B_j=R_j[[x]]$. Coefficientwise completeness of $R$ gives $\varprojlim_j B_j=R[[x]]=B$; multiplication agrees because each coefficient of a product is a finite sum. Thus $(F_j)_j$ determines $F\in B$. By Step 4, multiplication by $F_j$ is injective in $B_j$. Consequently the transition maps of $K_j=(F_j)$ are onto, and multiplication by $F_j$ identifies the tower $(K_j)$ with $(B_j)$, since $F_{j+1}$ reduces to $F_j$. Apply the cited inverse-limit exactness theorem to $0\to K_j\to B_j\to Q_j\to0$. It gives an onto map $B\to\varprojlim_jQ_j$ with kernel the image of $\varprojlim_jK_j$, which under the preceding tower identifications is exactly $FB$. Hence $\varprojlim_jQ_j\cong R[[x]]/(F)$ with all the chosen reductions. By Step 4 over the complete base this quotient is flat; it is complete Noetherian local as well.

source.place: Tag 03CA (lemma-Mittag-Leffler), applied to the principal-ideal kernel tower

proof.text: For the differential assertions work over either base in the statement. Write $B=R[[x]]$, $J=\mathfrak m_RB+(x)$, $Q=B/(F)$ and $\mathfrak n=JQ$. Let $M$ be a finite $Q$-module complete and separated for $\mathfrak n$. For $v=(v_i)\in M^n$, the formula $D_v(h)=\sum_i(\partial_i h)v_i$ is an $R$-derivation $B\to M$, since each formal partial derivative is the derivation in the cited definition. It is continuous: $\partial_i(J^{r+1})\subseteq J^r$ by Leibniz, as $\partial_i$ kills $\mathfrak m_R$ and sends each variable to $0$ or $1$. Conversely, truncate any series $h$ in total $x$-degree. Its polynomial truncations converge to $h$, and their partial derivatives converge to $\partial_i h$, because the omitted terms have degrees at least $s$ and their derivatives at least $s-1$. Any continuous $R$-derivation therefore agrees with $D_v$ on all series once it has the values $v_i$ on $x_i$: polynomial Leibniz gives the equality on truncations and separatedness of $M$ gives it on their limits. Thus evaluation on the coordinates is a bijection with $M^n$.

source.place: Examples of Deformation Problems Tag 0DY5, proof (1), formal derivative calculation; agent expansion by polynomial truncations

proof.text: The derivation $D_v$ of Step 8 descends to $Q=B/(F)$ exactly when $D_v(F)=\sum_i(\partial_iF)v_i=0$: indeed $D_v(Fh)=F D_v(h)+hD_v(F)$, with $F$ acting by zero on $M$. The quotient topology is the maximal-ideal topology, since the surjection sends $J^r$ onto $\mathfrak n^r$, so descended derivations are continuous. Put $P=\operatorname{coker}(Q\xrightarrow{(\partial_iF)_i}Q^n)$. A $Q$-linear map $P\to M$ is exactly a tuple $v_i$ satisfying the preceding relation. The derivation $\delta:Q\to P$, $h\mapsto[(\partial_i h)_i]$, is well defined by the same Leibniz calculation. The finite module $P$ is complete over the complete Noetherian local ring $Q$ by the cited finite-module completeness result. Every linear map of these adic modules is continuous, since it sends $\mathfrak n^rP$ into $\mathfrak n^rM$. Hence composition with $\delta$ gives the required natural bijection between $\operatorname{Hom}_Q(P,M)$ and continuous relative derivations.

source.place: Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3), and the universal-derivation calculation from Examples of Deformation Problems Tag 0DY5

proof.text: Finally set $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $C=\widehat A\cong R[[x]]/(F)$, and $L=\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_A C$. On an affine neighbourhood finite presentation makes its ring a finite-type $R$-algebra; the Noetherian finite-type and localization results give that $A$ is Noetherian. The differential sheaf theorem and localization of differentials identify $\Omega_{X/R,x}=\Omega_{A/R}$ and make it finite. Thus $L$ is finite and complete over $C$. The module-valued derivation-completion theorem, together with the finite-module completion/tensor comparison, extends $d:A\to\Omega_{A/R}$ uniquely to a continuous $R$-derivation $\widehat d:C\to L$. Step 9 gives a $C$-linear map $u:P\to L$ with $u\delta=\widehat d$. In the other direction restrict $\delta$ to $A$; the universal property of Kähler differentials gives $\Omega_{A/R}\to P$, and scalar extension gives $v:L\to P$. The continuous derivations $v\widehat d$ and $\delta$ agree on the dense image of $A$, hence agree on $C$. Therefore $vu$ fixes every $\delta(x_i)$, which generate $P$, so $vu=1$. Also $uv$ fixes every $da\otimes1$ for $a\in A$, which generate $L$, so $uv=1$. This identifies $L$ with the stated Jacobian-column cokernel, canonically relative to the specified formal coordinates.

The delivery creates no new nodes. Its statement and stmt_deps are identical to the live base (unsplit there, empty proof), and there is no repair note, so this is a first split. Steps 1-3: the universal property applies to the complete ring Q with q_i in m_Q, and its uniqueness clause shows the reduction mod m is the quotient map.
